sections.heading: What are Hungarian Subject Pronouns?
paragraphs: In Hungarian, subject pronouns (I, you, he/she, etc.) exist just like in English, but they are often left out because the verb ending already shows who the subject is.
Hungarian is therefore a “pro-drop” language, meaning you can omit the subject if it is clear from context.

sections.heading: Important Notes
list: Hungarian is a “pro-drop” language — subject pronouns can be left out.
The verb ending already shows the subject, so “tanulok” means “I study” even without “én”.
Pronouns are used mainly for emphasis or clarity.

sections.heading: Examples
list: Én főzök. – I am the one who is cooking (emphasis).
Ők mennek moziba. – They are going to the cinema.
Beszélsz magyarul? – Do you speak Hungarian?
Tanulunk minden nap. – We study every day.
